title: Concurrent whole-performance instructions with persistent voice clocks
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Whole multi-voice performance instructions generate timed events using separate persistent voice clocks, explicit entry synchronization, rests and bounded repeat descriptions. The text can order independent instructions differently while denoting the same performance; same-voice order and synchronization dependencies cannot be exchanged freely.

design.mechanism: Whole multi-voice performance instructions generate timed events using separate persistent voice clocks, explicit entry synchronization, rests and bounded repeat descriptions. The text can order independent instructions differently while denoting the same performance; same-voice order and synchronization dependencies cannot be exchanged freely.

source.work: Reading Rota, Harley978 f11v, mid13th-century source; current native inventory and rules already owned
source.ownership: 97 notated events:73 melody notes+6 pauses, and8 notes+1 pause in each pes. Complete owned matrix, operative rules and notation conflicts retained; no new original-image inspection this turn.

design.complete_scope: A full musical instruction program plus the complete generated melody/pes event streams in its declared finite execution window; not a translation of both English and Latin lyric texts. Whole score can be referenced as a defined motif, but every referenced event must be owned rather than an opaque arbitrary string.
source_constraints: One rota singer begins with both pes performers.
The next rota singer starts when the preceding singer reaches the first note after the cross, MN010;2–4 rota singers plus2 pes performers are source-permitted cases.
Only written pauses are used; upper pes pauses at end, lower pes in middle and not at end.
Pes repeat as needed. The source gives no unique stopping time or finite repeat count.
All native duration disagreements remain: four existing conditional branches are sensitivities, not an exhaustive certified edition; no branch is chosen to improve a code.

semantic_kernel.state: Per voice: persistent identity, local clock, current motif position and event log; explicit synchronization edges connect source-prescribed entries.
semantic_kernel.event: PLAY(voice,pitch,duration) or REST(voice,duration) appends at that voice local time and advances only that clock.
semantic_kernel.dependency: Same-voice events are ordered. ENTRY for a new singer depends on the previous singer reaching the specified cross-owned event. Cross-voice events commute only when no such dependency intervenes.
semantic_kernel.comparison: Compare complete voice-indexed timed interval/rest logs or their independently justified equivalence, not merely total note counts or literal character conjugacy.
semantic_kernel.bounded_control_policy: Use each fixed source duration interpretation separately; finite windows/repeat choices must be declared before any experiment. No full numeric source realization is newly certified here.

concrete_contrasts: A single global clock serializes positive-duration events and cannot reproduce the source-required initial simultaneity of first singer and both pes; preserving all pitches and counts does not fix that error.
Exchanging independent instructions on different voices leaves complete per-voice timed logs unchanged; exchanging different consecutive notes on one voice changes its timed pitch log.
Moving an entry synchronization across the source cross changes later overlap, even if each isolated voice retains the same melody.

generated_complete_control.status: modern two-voice finite illustration only; not a historical score excerpt
generated_complete_control.allowed_serializations: All6 interleavings preserving each voice order produce the same two timed logs.
generated_complete_control.same_voice_rival: Swap A notes while retaining their pitch-duration pairs: A has D during[0,1) then C during[1,3), differing from baseline C[0,2),D[2,3).
generated_complete_control.global_clock_rival: Every sequential realization consumes total6 units and cannot have both first notes begin at0; separate clocks finish both voices at3.

design.novelty_relative_142: IDEA142 already owns broad coordinated-voice meaning and all source cautions. The proposed added mechanism is nonliteral concurrent instruction semantics with a fixed dependence relation and complete-log equivalence, not another named music genre or counterpoint rule. This raw descendant adds neither a target part owner nor a surface code.
design.retained_primary: GDT970 REPORT read fully: the fixed concatenated whole-pes event code has no literal paragraph pair; the failure occurs at lengths/counts, before ordering. It remains closed. This raw proposal does not reopen its paragraph pairing, swap duration branches, relax a code or rerun a projected-string screen. A future concurrent-language test needs its own complete grammar and a genuinely different consequence.
likely_failure: Without independently bounded voices and entry relations, arbitrary track assignment can absorb nearly any sequence.
A guessed dependence graph can make every inconvenient event commute; the relation must be globally fixed by voice identity and explicit synchronization semantics.
Current duration certification and initialization audit limits remain. Earlier steady-period execution is not initialization evidence.
Commuting program descriptions do not prove that historical writing used such interleaving.
No universal consonance law is supplied or invented; generic delayed melodies alone are weak evidence.
design.data_needed: Whole passage/channel ownership, fixed finite participant/motif/reference grammar, typed duration representation, independently constrained simultaneity or entry relations, and full-program comparisons against one-clock and wrong-dependence rivals. Known words are not prerequisites for an exploratory joint model.
